<reason>CON (A) won a close debate by making substitution the live cost of the cap and breaking PRO’s claim that fringe lenders already exist beside cards, so leakage does not matter. A showed a binding cap expands that worse pool and that PRO’s sympathetic emergency borrower is the person rationed out. B had punchier rhetoric, a cleaner “motion already prices in lost access” rule, and a surviving remaining-borrower benefit (slower compounding), but never neutralized the uncontested worse-product channel. A’s clipped opening and closing kept the margin thin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s reply that payday/title markets currently serve people who cannot get a card at any price, so a cap adds marginal borrowers to that pool rather than leaving substitution unchanged.</best_rebuttal>
